summary: An older helper script that packages the app into one Windows program using PyInstaller.
purpose: Creates a standalone program file for teammates who do not run Python themselves.
why: Unclear. The closing message recommends a simpler deployment approach, which suggests this method was set aside. Reason not fully stated in the code.
how: Old build folders are removed. PyInstaller is then run on the backend entry file, with the backend folder, the environment example file and many libraries bundled in. When it finishes, the script prints where the program should be and points to a deployment guide.
inputs: No inputs. It reads project files from the folder it is run in.
outputs: A program file at dist/UniversalRAG.exe if PyInstaller succeeds, plus messages in the console.
risks: The bundling entries use a colon as the separator, which is the Linux and Mac form, so bundling may fail on Windows. It starts from the backend entry file rather than the launcher used by the newer build script. It deletes build and dist folders without asking. The message points to a guide file that may not exist.
debug: If the build fails, check the separator used in the bundling entries. If the program does not start, compare with the approach in build_standalone.py. Confirm the deployment guide exists.
